lessons.title: Colours
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam share fruit with Smarty. Practise naming colours; no personal details are needed.

items.note: Use red to say what colour a thing is, like a tomato.

image.describe: a single red apple, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.note: Use blue to say the colour of a thing, like a happy bird.

image.describe: a single blue bird sitting on a branch, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.note: Use green for things like a green apple.

image.describe: a single green apple with a leaf, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.note: Use yellow for things like a banana.

image.describe: a single yellow banana, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.note: Use black for dark things, like Smarty the cat.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat sitting calmly, solid black ink, no colour in the picture

practice.prompt: Mia has a banana. What does she say?
practice.explanation: A banana is yellow, so yellow goes after the word is.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour word after is.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: The colour comes at the end: It is blue.

practice.prompt: Smarty is the colour of dark ink. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Smarty is a black cat, so black fits.

practice.prompt: Match the colour with the thing that usually has it.
practice.explanation: A tomato is red, a banana is yellow, water looks blue and Smarty is black.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence, including the small word is.

practice.prompt: Mia says: I like the green apple. What does Mia like?
practice.explanation: Green tells us which apple Mia likes.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for both the colour and the pet.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Say the colour before the thing: the yellow banana.

story.hook: Mia has an apple. Is it red?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello, Sam! I have an apple.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I have a banana. It is yellow.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! I am black and the banana is yellow.

questions.explanation: Mia says: No, it is green.
Sam says: I have a banana.
Smarty says: I am black.

image.describe: A sunny table with a green apple and a yellow banana; Mia and Sam sit at it and Smarty the black cat watches.

mission.setup: Smarty is at the fruit table with you. Say what you have, using a colour.

turns.smarty: I have a banana. And you?
turns.hint: Say I have, then a colour and a thing.

turns.smarty: I like yellow. And you?
turns.hint: Say I like and one colour.

lessons.title: What colour is it?
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam show new bags to Smarty. Practise asking and answering about colours.

items.note: Use white for things like milk.

image.describe: a glass of milk drawn with a thin ink outline, the milk left blank white, no other colour

items.note: Use pink for a light red colour, like a pink dress.

image.describe: a single pink balloon, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.note: Use purple for things like a purple bag.

image.describe: a single purple bag, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.note: Use brown for things like brown bread.

image.describe: a single brown loaf of bread, the only coloured thing in the picture

items.example: What colour is it? It is red.
items.note: Ask What colour is it? to find out the colour of a thing.

practice.prompt: You want to know a colour. Which question do you ask?
practice.explanation: What colour is it? asks about the colour of a thing.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour at the end.

practice.prompt: Build the question in the right order.
practice.explanation: The question is What colour is it?

practice.prompt: Think of a cold drink from a cow. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Milk is white.

practice.prompt: Match the colour with the thing that usually has it.
practice.explanation: Milk is white, a tomato is red, a banana is yellow and bread is brown.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say all three words: What colour is it?

practice.prompt: Sam asks about the banana. Choose the best answer.
practice.explanation: Answer the colour question with It is and a colour.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Say the colour before the thing.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for blue after the word is.

story.hook: Two friends have new bags. Are they the same colour?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Sam, I have a new bag.

questions.explanation: Mia says: It is brown.

questions.prompt: Who has a pink and white bag?
questions.explanation: Sam says: It is pink and white.
Smarty says: I like pink!

image.describe: Mia and Sam each hold a new bag; Smarty the black cat looks at them. One bag is brown, the other pink and white.

mission.setup: You and Smarty talk about bags. Ask about the colour, then say the colour of your own bag.

turns.smarty: Hello! I have a new bag.
turns.hint: Ask the colour question.

turns.smarty: It is purple. What colour is your bag?
turns.hint: Say It is and a colour.

lessons.title: Clothes
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam talk about clothes in their bags. Practise naming clothes and their colours.

items.note: A shirt is clothes for your top half. Say shirts for more than one.

image.describe: a single plain shirt with a collar and buttons on a hanger

items.note: A T-shirt is a short shirt with no collar.

image.describe: a single T-shirt with short sleeves laid flat

items.note: Trousers always ends in s. Say The trousers are, not The trousers is.

image.describe: a pair of trousers hanging over a chair back

items.note: A dress is one piece of clothes. Say dresses for more than one.

image.describe: a single simple dress on a hanger

items.note: Shoes are a pair, so say The shoes are.

image.describe: a pair of shoes side by side on the floor

practice.prompt: Mia has black trousers. What does she say?
practice.explanation: Trousers are a pair, so we say are.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for shoes and the colour.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: One dress takes is.

practice.prompt: Choose the right small word.
practice.explanation: Trousers is a pair, so we say are.

practice.prompt: Match one thing with more than one.
practice.explanation: Shirts, dresses and T-shirts end in s. A shoe is one of a pair of shoes.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence, with a before T-shirt.

practice.prompt: Complete the question.
practice.explanation: To ask about colour, say What colour is it?

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.answer: I have a white shirt and black shoes.
practice.explanation: Put each colour before its clothes.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour and the clothes.

story.hook: Sam and Mia have bags full of clothes. What is in them?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: A white shirt and black trousers.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: A pink dress and brown shoes.

questions.explanation: Mia says: A pink dress and brown shoes.
Sam says: A white shirt and black trousers.
Mia says: A pink dress and brown shoes.

image.describe: Sam and Mia sit on the floor with open bags; a white shirt, black trousers, a pink dress and brown shoes lie beside them.

mission.setup: You open your bag with Smarty. Say what clothes you have and their colour.

turns.smarty: I have a bag. What do you have?
turns.hint: Say I have and the clothes.

turns.smarty: What colour is it?
turns.hint: Say the colour.

lessons.title: I'm wearing a hat
lessons.scenario: Smarty asks Mia and Sam what they are wearing. Practise saying what you are wearing.

items.example: I am wearing a blue hat.
items.note: Say I am wearing, or I’m wearing, to tell what clothes you have on now.

items.example: I am wearing a black jacket.
items.note: A jacket is clothes you wear on top when it is cool.

image.describe: a single jacket with a zip on a hanger

items.example: Mia is wearing a pink hat.
items.note: A hat goes on your head.

image.describe: a single hat with a brim sitting on a table

items.note: Socks are a pair, so we say socks.

image.describe: a pair of socks side by side

practice.prompt: You have a hat on your head. What do you say?
practice.explanation: I am wearing tells what clothes you have on, here a hat.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: I’m wearing is the short way to say I am wearing.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: I am wearing comes first, then the clothes.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word.
practice.explanation: Wearing goes after I am when you tell what clothes you have on.

practice.prompt: Match the long form with the short form.
practice.explanation: Each short form joins the two words with an apostrophe.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say all four words: I am wearing, then a hat.

practice.prompt: Mia says: I am wearing a black jacket. What is black?
practice.explanation: Black comes just before jacket, so the jacket is black.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: She is wearing a pink dress.
practice.answer: She is wearing a pink dress.
options: She is wearing a pink dress.
She is wearing a pink hat.
She is wearing a brown dress.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour and the clothes.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word.
practice.explanation: He goes with is.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.answer: You are wearing a white shirt.
practice.explanation: You goes with are.

story.hook: Smarty is looking at his friends. Who has a hat?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hi, Mia! What are you wearing?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I am wearing a pink hat.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Smarty, you are not wearing a hat!

questions.explanation: Mia says: I am wearing a pink hat.

questions.prompt: Who is wearing a black jacket?
questions.explanation: Sam says: I’m wearing a black jacket.
Smarty says: I am wearing socks!

image.describe: Mia in a pink hat and Sam in a black jacket stand outside; Smarty the black cat wears little socks.

mission.setup: Smarty asks about your clothes today. Say what you are wearing. You can use an imaginary outfit.

turns.smarty: What are you wearing?
turns.hint: Say I am wearing and the clothes.

turns.smarty: I am wearing a hat. Are you wearing a hat?
turns.hint: Say Yes, I am or No, I am not.

lessons.title: Too long!
lessons.scenario: Mia tries a coat in a shop. Practise saying that clothes do not fit.

items.note: Use too before a word like big or small to say it is a problem.
Use long when something is a lot of length, like a long coat.

image.describe: a very long coat that touches the floor on a hanger

items.note: Size tells how big or small clothes are for you.
A coat is warm clothes you wear outside.

image.describe: a single thick warm coat with big buttons on a hanger

grammar.title: too + adjective
grammar.explanation: Put too before big, small, long or short to say it is more than you want: The coat is too long.

practice.prompt: Ben’s coat touches the floor. What does he say?
practice.explanation: Too long says the coat is more long than you want.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for big and small.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Too comes just before long.

practice.prompt: Sam is tall. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Tall Sam needs longer trousers, so the trousers are too short.

practice.prompt: Match the words that mean the opposite.
practice.explanation: Big and small, long and short, hot and cold are opposites.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence, with too before long.

practice.prompt: Choose the question about size.
practice.explanation: Size is the word for how big or small something is.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: The brown coat is too big.
practice.answer: The brown coat is too big.
options: The brown coat is too big.
The brown coat is too small.
The black coat is too big.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour and for big.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: My goes before jacket.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: I am wearing a hat but it is too big.
practice.answer: I am wearing a hat but it is too big.
options: I am wearing a hat but it is too big.
I am wearing a hat but it is too small.
I am wearing a hat but it is too long.
practice.explanation: But joins the two ideas.

story.hook: Mia tries a big brown coat in the shop. Does it fit?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: It is brown. Is it your size?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Here you are, Mia. This coat is size six.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Thank you, Zara! It is not too long.

questions.prompt: What colour is the first coat?
questions.explanation: Sam says: It is brown.

questions.prompt: What does Mia say about the first coat?
questions.explanation: Mia says: No, it is too long.

questions.prompt: Who says: Here you are, Mia?
questions.explanation: Zara gives Mia the new coat.

image.describe: In a clothes shop Mia wears a very long brown coat that touches the floor; Sam and the shop helper Zara stand beside her.

mission.setup: You are in a shop with Smarty. Say whether the clothes are your size.

turns.smarty: This coat is very long. Is it your size?
turns.hint: Say No, it is too long, or Yes.

turns.smarty: This jacket is small. Is it your size?
turns.hint: Say if it is too small or too big.

lessons.title: Whose is this?
lessons.scenario: A scarf is lost on the table at school. Practise asking whose it is and answering.

items.example: Whose is this? It is a scarf.
items.note: Ask Whose is this? when you find a thing and want to know who has it.
Use mine to say a thing belongs to you.
Use yours to say a thing belongs to the person you talk to.
A scarf goes around your neck when it is cold.

image.describe: a single long scarf folded on a table

practice.prompt: A hat is on the table. Ask who has it.
practice.explanation: Whose is this? asks who a thing belongs to.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Mine means it belongs to the speaker.

practice.prompt: Build the question in the right order.
practice.explanation: Whose comes first in the question.

practice.prompt: Mia says: This is my scarf. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Mia owns the scarf, so it is mine.

practice.prompt: Match the sentence with the owner word.
practice.explanation: My goes with mine, your goes with yours, his stays his.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say all three words: Whose is this?

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Her means it belongs to a girl.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: This is points at the thing.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Your goes with yours.

story.hook: A scarf is on the table. Whose is it?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: It is a scarf. It is pink.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes! It is mine. Thank you!

questions.explanation: Mia says: It is pink.

questions.prompt: Who says: No, it is not mine?
questions.explanation: Sam says it is not his scarf.
Ana says: It is mine.

image.describe: A pink scarf lies on a school table; Ben, Mia, Sam and Ana stand around it while Smarty the black cat watches.

mission.setup: You find a scarf with Smarty. Answer his questions about whose it is.

turns.smarty: This is a scarf. Is it yours?
turns.hint: Say Yes, it is mine or No, it is not mine.

turns.smarty: Whose is this?
turns.hint: Say It is mine or It is yours.

lessons.title: I want new boots
lessons.scenario: Mia and Leo look in a shop window with Smarty. Practise saying what you want.

items.note: Say I want and a thing to tell what you would like to have.
Boots are a pair of strong shoes, so we say boots.

image.describe: a pair of tall boots standing side by side

items.note: Jeans are like trousers: we always say jeans, and The jeans are.

image.describe: a pair of jeans hanging over a chair back

items.note: A skirt hangs from your waist. Say skirts for more than one.

image.describe: a single skirt on a hanger

practice.prompt: You would like new boots. What do you say?
practice.explanation: I want tells what you would like to have.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour and the clothes.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: I want comes first, then the thing.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word. You would like new boots.
practice.explanation: Want tells what you would like.

practice.prompt: Which word is always plural, like trousers?
practice.explanation: We always say jeans, like trousers.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence, including a before skirt.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the colour.

practice.prompt: Build the question in the right order.
practice.answer: Can I have the red boots?
practice.explanation: Can I have is a polite way to ask for something.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: These points at more than one thing.

story.hook: Leo and Mia look at a shop. What do they want?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Hi, Mia! I want new boots.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I want black boots. And you?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I want a pink skirt and blue jeans.

questions.explanation: Leo says: I want new boots, black boots.
Mia says: I want a pink skirt.
Smarty says: I want new socks!

image.describe: Leo and Mia stand outside a clothes shop window full of boots, jeans and skirts; Smarty the black cat sits between them.

mission.setup: You are at a shop window with Smarty. Say what clothes you want.

turns.smarty: I want new boots. What do you want?
turns.hint: Say I want and the clothes.

turns.smarty: What colour?
turns.hint: Say the colour you want.

lessons.title: Getting dressed
lessons.scenario: Mia gets dressed on a cold morning with Smarty. Practise talking about putting clothes on and taking them off.

items.note: Use put on when you start to wear clothes. Say puts on for he or she.

image.describe: a child in the middle of putting on a jacket, one arm in the sleeve

items.note: Use take off when you stop wearing clothes. Say takes off for he or she.

image.describe: a child sitting taking shoes off, shoes beside their feet

items.note: Gloves are a pair, so we say gloves.

image.describe: a pair of gloves lying side by side

items.note: A belt goes around your trousers.

image.describe: a single belt with a buckle coiled on a table

practice.prompt: It is cold. What do you do?
practice.explanation: Put on starts the wearing.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Take off means you stop wearing them.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Put on comes before my gloves.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word.
practice.explanation: For he or she we say puts on.

practice.prompt: Match each phrase with its form for he or she.
practice.explanation: For he or she we add s: puts, takes, gets, washes, eats.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say put on as two words.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for put on, not take off.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.answer: I get up and put on my T-shirt.
practice.explanation: First you get up, then you put on your clothes.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word.
practice.text: I put on a black ___ and my trousers.
practice.explanation: A belt goes around your trousers.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word.
practice.explanation: For Mia we say takes off.

story.hook: It is a cold morning. What does Mia put on?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning, Mia. It is cold.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I put on my jacket and gloves.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I put on my black belt too.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: At home, I take off my jacket.

questions.prompt: What does Mia put on first?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I put on my jacket and gloves.

questions.prompt: What does Mia take off at home?
questions.explanation: Mia says: At home, I take off my jacket.
Mia says: I put on my black belt.

image.describe: Mia at home in the morning putting on a jacket and gloves by the door while Smarty the black cat watches; a belt hangs on a hook.

mission.setup: It is a cold morning and you talk with Smarty. Say what you put on, and then what you take off.

turns.smarty: It is cold. What do you put on?
turns.hint: Say I put on and your clothes.

turns.smarty: You are at home. What do you take off?
turns.hint: Say I take off and your clothes.

lessons.title: My favourite colour
lessons.scenario: Friends talk about favourite colours. Practise saying what colour you like best.

items.note: Your favourite is the one you like best.
Put dark before a colour to say it is deep, like dark blue.
Put light before a colour to say it is soft, like light blue.
Grey is a colour between black and white.

practice.prompt: Ask Ana which colour she likes best.
practice.explanation: Favourite means you like it best.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: My favourite colour is dark blue.
practice.answer: My favourite colour is dark blue.
options: My favourite colour is dark blue.
My favourite colour is light blue.
My favourite colour is dark green.
practice.explanation: Listen for dark or light.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: My favourite colour is comes before the colour.

practice.prompt: This is not dark pink. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Light is the opposite of dark.

practice.prompt: Match the words that mean the opposite.
practice.explanation: Dark and light, big and small, long and short, clean and dirty are opposites.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say all five words from My to green.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: I like the dark blue jacket.
practice.answer: I like the dark blue jacket.
options: I like the dark blue jacket.
I like the light blue jacket.
I like the dark blue coat.
practice.explanation: Listen for dark and for jacket.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: Light goes before the colour.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I love green. It is my ___ colour.
practice.explanation: The colour you love most is your favourite.

story.hook: Every friend has a favourite colour. What is Smarty’s?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Ben, what is your favourite colour?

lines.speaker: Ben

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: My favourite colour is light pink.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Smarty, what is your favourite colour?

questions.explanation: Ben says: My favourite colour is dark blue.

Smarty says: My favourite colour is grey!

image.describe: Mia and Ben sit with Smarty the black cat on a bench; each holds a coloured crayon-free ink drawing of a favourite thing, one dark, one light.

lessons.title: Fashion show
lessons.scenario: Smarty is in a clothes show with his friends. Practise saying how clothes look and describing an outfit.

items.note: Use look to say how a person or clothes seem: You look great.
Say great to say something is very good.
Say cool to say something is nice and fun.

items.example: The uniform is blue and white.
items.note: A uniform is the same clothes that many people wear, like at school.

image.describe: a child in a simple school uniform: shirt, tie and trousers, standing straight

practice.prompt: Say something nice to Mia about her dress.
practice.explanation: You look great! is a friendly thing to say about clothes.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for cool.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.explanation: For she we say looks.

practice.prompt: Pick the word for the same clothes everyone wears at school.
practice.explanation: A uniform is the same clothes for everyone at school.

practice.prompt: Match the words that mean the opposite.
practice.explanation: Put on and take off, dark and light, hot and cold, clean and dirty are opposites.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Say all three words: You look great.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: She is wearing a red hat and blue shoes.
practice.answer: She is wearing a red hat and blue shoes.
options: She is wearing a red hat and blue shoes.
She is wearing a red hat and black shoes.
She is wearing a pink hat and blue shoes.
practice.explanation: Listen for each colour and each thing.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right order.
practice.answer: I am wearing a black belt.
practice.explanation: Say the colour before belt.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word.
practice.text: Ben ___ cool in his new jacket.
practice.explanation: For Ben we say looks.

practice.prompt: Mia asks: Whose is this jacket? It is yours. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Mine means it belongs to you.

story.hook: Smarty is in a clothes show. What do his friends say?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello! I am wearing a new hat and a black jacket.

questions.answer: a new hat and a black jacket
options: a new hat and a black jacket
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I am wearing a new hat and a black jacket.

questions.prompt: What does Leo say about Smarty?
questions.explanation: Leo says: He looks great!
